result_json.notes: v1.4 re-estimates the Delivery Budget only; scope, phases, IDs, checklists, ACs, and DC0 are unchanged, and Phase 1 commits fa19978d/ce74d860 and its checked items are preserved. Using the prior plan review and the Phase 1 review as evidence: W7 goes from 3 to 5. The R3 closure correction (+1) sat only in run_a9914ec93486's final-corrections allowance (effective ceiling 25), which a new run does not inherit. The v1.2 arithmetic split also left the core turn loop at about 1 point. Combined W7 work re-estimates to 4, which is off-scale, so it is scored 5 rather than rounded down. W3 records its Phase 1 evidence (actual effort 1). W1, W2, W4, W5, W6, and W8 were checked against current code and are unchanged; none was lowered. Operator warning: the ledger now sums to 26, against the governing baseline B=18 (standard ceiling 23, absolute 27), with DC0 credit excluded as directed. The overage is 3 points over standard, up from 1. The overage cannot be honestly removed without a scope change such as dropping the doctor check (W4/AC2 evidence) or the live installed delegation exercise (R2 acceptance), and I made none. An explicit plan-review budget decision or a fresh independent baseline is needed. The reviewer's own independent estimate (20 initial + 7 effortDelta = 27) supports 26. No Governing decisions block was appended to the prompt, and no new-run review artifact existed. The plan-only factory-seam return-type and scanner-recovery nonblocking notes were left as-is because they are excluded from structured items.

result_json.message: docs: add plan review for OpenCode 2.x upgrade

items.title: Tie settlement to delivery of the submitted prompt
items.reason: V2 prompt admission returns an inbox item, while execution terminal events identify only the session. The prior turn can emit a terminal event before the new prompt is delivered.
items.failure: A resumed invocation can settle against the previous execution, return the wrong reply or usage, or send a summary prematurely.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Require delivery evidence for the exact inbox item before settling either path; reject an active or overlapping session when ownership cannot be established. Add a same-session prior-terminal-before-delivery regression.

items.title: Cancel pending work as well as running work
items.reason: Session interrupt does not remove a queued inbox item, and an aborted admission request can have committed before its acknowledgment is received.
items.failure: A cancelled external invocation can execute later, or interrupt a different execution.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Short-circuit a pre-aborted turn, assign a stable prompt ID before admission, and bound the RPCs. Cancel the owned pending item or interrupt the owned active execution, handling a delivery race. Add delayed-acknowledgment and queued-cancellation fixtures.

items.title: Route headless forms by their actual session discriminator
items.reason: The planned data.sessionID filter drops form.created, which carries sessionID and id under data.form.
items.failure: The headless fallback ignores its own pending form and the invocation stalls.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Extract the nested form session and ID, test own and foreign forms, and explicitly exercise question denial or the fallback in the live test.

items.title: Use an executable Phase 1 unit-test gate
items.reason: The Phase 1 review records nonzero exit from bare bun test test/unit on both revisions, and a passing run with the configured parallel flags.
items.failure: The literal required Phase 1 command cannot provide passing evidence on the reviewed tree.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Spell the previously passing configured unit command in the gate: bun test --concurrent --parallel=2 --dots --timeout 15000 test/unit.

items.title: Pipe managed stderr explicitly
items.reason: Bun inherits stderr by default for the specified spawn, which contradicts the bounded diagnostic capture and draining contract.
items.failure: Early startup errors lose the required stderr tail and child diagnostics bypass managed capture.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Specify piped stdout and stderr in the managed spawn options and assert both in the existing spawn-seam test.

items.title: Exercise real reviewer output through 5x invoke
items.reason: AC1 includes author and reviewer results, but the live provider schema and end-to-end invoke checks exercise only the author role.
items.failure: Both modes can pass the acceptance suite even if neither returns a CLI-validated reviewer verdict.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Seed a valid temp plan/run and run one unrecorded reviewer invoke in each existing mode fixture, checking role-specific ReviewerVerdict validation alongside the author checks.

items.title: Require positive live evidence for the advertised minimum
items.reason: The enabled live suite can skip on an unsuitable binary, and a test only on 2.4.2 does not verify the claimed 2.4.0 minimum.
items.failure: The release can claim compatibility with an unverified minimum or pass the opt-in gate without exercising either mode.
items.lowestCostCorrection: Fail bad prerequisites when opted in, require both cases on the advertised minimum or raise it to the oldest verified release, and align the old-2.x error with that minimum and the doctor upgrade hint.

result_json.summary: The W7 re-estimate is credible and DC0 is eligible at plan time, but the prior inherited-budget blocker is a CLI governance matter, not an estimate correction or a credit-carry guarantee. The plan needs mechanical corrections to turn ownership, cancellation, headless handling, and acceptance evidence before it is executable as written.

baselineAssessment.reason: Independent sizing by implementation boundary: private server/client and event mapper, asynchronous turn and recovery, structured extraction, factory and live validation, installed native delegation and harness sync, doctor, TUI deletion, and release verification. Server timing and the installed delegation exercise are the main uncertainties.

creditAssessments.reason: Removing the old SDK requires addressing its unused importers before provider typecheck. Deleting the retired attach, permission and routing path is simpler than porting it; the persisted phase-1 target and before/after evidence substantiate provisional plan eligibility, not execution carry.
